subject.title: [Feature]: Add optional capability descriptors to tool definitions

question: Should OpenClaw add a public per-tool behavioral capability descriptor contract, and what taxonomy and trust semantics should plugins, built-in tools, Gateway projections, and policy hooks use?
rationale: Automation can verify the API gap, but choosing security-policy metadata semantics for third-party plugins is a maintainer security and product contract decision.

options.title: Design a unified descriptor contract
options.body: Define an additive versioned descriptor object, unknown-by-default semantics, advisory plugin declarations, built-in tool declarations, Gateway projection, hook exposure, docs, and contract tests before implementation.

options.title: Fold into broader permissions work
options.body: Keep this issue open but make the descriptor taxonomy part of the broader capability-based permissions and action-provenance design before any standalone PR.

options.title: Defer until Security Matrix direction lands
options.body: Wait for the Security Matrix and audit model direction to settle, then decide whether this descriptor layer should feed that model or stay separate.

recommendation.title: Design a unified descriptor contract
recommendation.body: Define an additive versioned descriptor object, unknown-by-default semantics, advisory plugin declarations, built-in tool declarations, Gateway projection, hook exposure, docs, and contract tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the adjacent trusted policy and plugin tool metadata SDK surfaces that this proposal would extend.
